Read out of saint.gr's line for 12 Ιουλίου, «Άγιοι Πρόκλος και Ιλάριος», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 12. јул ст. ст., „Св. муч. Прокл и Иларије.“ — „Св. муч.“ is the rank, which `types` already carries, and the heading enumerates two bare forenames with no by-name, no place and no see; «of Callippi» in the display name is the corpus’s own, off the body. `foldchk.py` returns no holder and `sr-foldpred.mjs` predicts a new key with no other holder, which on a bare forename of five letters is the day’s one piece of luck — the companion’s form was not so fortunate.
Name page 1838 is «Прокл Калиптский, мч.»; the rank is stripped. The day line declines him as «Прокла» and gives no epithet at all, so the name page is where the epithet is read.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 12 июля ст. ст. — «Мчч. Прокла и Илария (II).»

attestations.note: The day's first entry, two names on one line and two folders already held, both `undocumented`. The epithet settles them: name pages 1838 and 925 are «Прокл Калиптский, мч.» and «Иларий Калиптский, мч.», which is the Callippi of both display names, and the century «(II)» agrees with the Romanian, Greek and Serbian rows already on this same menologion day. `dates` unchanged — this folder has none, and «(II)» would be its first, off a Roman numeral. The reading life4220 was NOT opened. The day page prints one kontakion for the two of them and it names them both; it is taken in both folders.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 12 iulie — «Sfântul Mucenic Proclu»

attestations.note: The day prints the two men on separate lines, each with its own copy of one shared life, so the corpus keeps one folder for each. The life itself dates Hilary's death to 15 July, three days after Proclus's, and the Romanian calendar keeps them both on 12 iulie.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 12ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιοι Πρόκλος και Ιλάριος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 12 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the Greek line pairs the same two men the Romanian one does — «Sfântul Mucenic Proclu» and «Sfântul Mucenic Ilarie» against «Άγιοι Πρόκλος και Ιλάριος». The pairing and the day settle him against the corpus's five other men of the name. The Greek page adds the reign the Romanian did not — the emperor Trajan, which it brackets 98 to 117, and the governor Maximus — and the manner of his death, the arrows. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page prints two apolytikia: the first names both men and is taken, and the second is the common of several martyrs «Οἱ Μάρτυρες σου Κύριε», printed under their name, which is taken as a common and said here to be one.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 25.07.2026 (12. јул ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Прокл и Иларије.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry, an **enumerated pair both of whose folders this corpus holds and already relates in both directions**, which is the easiest shape this source produces and the third time this range has met it. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, with its closing full stop, which is what §4 asks for and what `srbody.mjs` now hands back. The identification is the place and the kinship and the day: „Ови мученици беху родом из Калипте у Азији“ is this folder’s own Callippi, „и Прокл беше стриц Иларију“ — Proclus was Hilary’s paternal uncle — is the relation the two folders already record, and the Romanian and Greek rows stand on this very 12 July. **`dates` STAY NULL, AND THE REIGN IS WHY.** The folder holds no `dates` at all and this book offers „Пострадаше у време Трајаново“, they suffered in the time of Trajan. **A reign is no source for a year** — the rule that refused a year off Decius’s reign and off the reign of Michael and Theodora on 9 July, and off Julian the Apostate before that — and Trajan’s reign would in any case have to be looked up outside this book, which is the whole of the objection. Written into the life, written into no field. `types` UNTOUCHED at `martyr`, which „муч.“ is and all the heading gives. No `locations`: Callippi in Asia is a narrative. No new `related` rows — the two are already two-way, and the judge who sentenced them is unnamed. **WHAT IS NEW IS TWO SPEECHES.** Asked „Каквога си рода?“, of what family are you, Proclus answered „Род је мој Христос, и надежда моја Бог мој“ — my family is Christ, and my hope is my God. Threatened with torments he answered that if his judges feared to transgress the emperor’s command lest they fall into short-lasting torments, how much more do Christians fear to transgress the command of God lest they fall into eternal ones. And **the two deaths are different deaths**: Proclus was crucified and Hilary beheaded with the sword. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. **ENTRY 5 IS A FATHER AND A SON AND NEITHER HAS A FOLDER.** „Св. муч. Теодор и Јован.“ — „Отац и син, по пореклу Варјази, који беху крштени па се доселише у незнабожни град Кијев да живе. Јаросни незнабошци срушише кућу над њима, те обојица погибоше за Христа. Њихове се мошти покоје у Антонијевим пештерама. Њима се највише моле бездетни и они којима се деца не држе.“ — a father and a son, Varangians by descent, who were baptised and then settled in the pagan city of Kyiv to live; furious pagans pulled the house down on them and both perished for Christ; their relics rest in Anthony’s caves; and those who pray to them most are the childless and those whose children do not live. `ls saints | grep -i varangian` returns **nobody**, and the corpus holds scores of Theodores and scores of Johns without one of Kyiv who died with his son under a house. Ruling 3: **reported, not created.** The entry is four sentences and this book is the only calendar of the four that prints them — and the refusal has a cost that will be visible three days later, because the Julian 15 July’s entry on Vladimir says the church of the Most Holy Theotokos at Kyiv was raised „на оном истом месту, где раније мученички пострадаше за Христа св. Теодор и син му Јован (в. 12. јули)“ — on the very place where Theodore and his son John had earlier suffered — so the pair are named twice in this range and hold no folder either time.

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfinților Mucenici Proclu și Ilarie», Glasul 4 — the common troparion of martyrs, printed here for the two of them; the spelling «nesctricăciunii» is the page's own

english.text: Your martyrs, Lord, in their struggles received from You, our God, the crowns of incorruption; for having Your strength they overthrew their torturers and broke the powerless insolence of the demons. At their prayers, Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Σταυροῦ τὴν πανοπλίαν ἱερῶς ἐνδυσάμενοι, Ἰλάριε καὶ Πρόκλε, ὑπὲρ φύσιν ἠθλήσατε, καὶ δόξης οὐρανίου κοινωνοί, ἐδείχθητε ὡς μέτοχοι Χριστοῦ, διὰ τοῦτο χαρισμάτων ταὶς δωρεαίς, πυρσεύετε τοὺς κράζοντας, δόξα τῷ ἐνισχύσαντι ὑμᾶς, δόξα τῷ στεφανώοαντι, δόξα τῷ ἐνεργούντι δι' ὑμῶν πάσιν ἰάματα.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος ἀ’, Τῆς ἐρήμου πολίτης — the first of two apolytikia on the shared page of «Άγιοι Πρόκλος και Ιλάριος», and it names them both

english.text: Having sacredly put on the full armour of the Cross, Hilary and Proclus, you contended beyond nature, and were shown sharers of heavenly glory as partakers of Christ; and so by the gifts of your graces you set alight those who cry: Glory to him who strengthened you, glory to him who crowned you, glory to him who works healings for all through you.

hymns.text: Οἱ Μάρτυρες σου Κύριε, ἐν τῇ ἀθλήσει αὐτῶν, τὸ στέφος ἐκομίσαντο τῆς ἀφθαρσίας, ἐκ σοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν· σχόντες γὰρ τὴν ἰσχύν σου, τοὺς τυράννους καθεῖλον· ἔθραυσαν καὶ δαιμόνων τὰ ἀνίσχυρα θράση. Αὐτῶν ταῖς ἱκεσίαις Χριστὲ ὁ Θεός, σῶσον τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχύ προκατάλαβε — the second apolytikion on the shared page of the two. It is the common of several martyrs, printed under their name and naming nobody else, and is copied as the page has it

english.text: Your martyrs, O Lord, in their contending received from you our God the crown of incorruption; for having your strength they brought down the tyrants, and shattered the powerless insolence of the demons. By their entreaties, Christ our God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Яко денница звезда, возсия/ мучеников Прокла и Илария/ честное страдание,/ предозаряющи нас чудес светлостьми./ Темже празднуем память вашу:/ Христа Бога молите,// да спасет души наша.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 12 июля ст. ст. — «Кондак мучеников Прокла и Илария», глас 4

english.text: Like the morning star, the honourable suffering of the martyrs Proclus and Hilary has shone forth, enlightening us beforehand with the brightness of wonders. Therefore we keep your memory: pray to Christ God that He may save our souls.
